analysis.title: GS flow and positioning observations
key_insights: Futures sharply higher on 11/19 driven by NDX, but Asia is weak. A TSMC-exposed basket is down 8% and Asian data center names are under pressure after new BIS rules.

New BIS rules tighten advanced AI chip licensing across parts of Asia and Brazil and restrict offshore compute access for Chinese customers. The desk says this was not fully priced in Asia, though two months of aggressive selling have left global semis valuations depressed, so it takes little good news to squeeze.
Rates rallied despite a hawkish Waller, Fed minutes and ECB regulatory noise. The back end was well bid, the curve bull flattened and the front end was broadly unchanged.
Australia posted a big jobs miss. The 2-year yield rallied hard and cuts started to price, which the desk reads as potentially signaling the end of the hiking cycle.

The desk sees the market pricing weaker growth as capex expectations fall, commodities roll over and inflation pressure fades. It draws parallels to the end of 2018: a late-cycle slowdown with very different policy implications.

Gold and precious metals face competition from a strong dollar, elevated real rates and attractive credit yields. The desk calls it a spending glut rather than a savings glut, a less supportive backdrop for precious metals with the Fed tightening.

China is a further headwind: weak growth, Shanghai equities near lows and potential restrictions on AI/data center investment. Copper has become a proxy for the AI theme, and its resilience is hard to reconcile with collapsing AI infrastructure equities.
Precious and industrial metals, grains, gasoline and diesel are all under pressure. The desk sees a broad disinflationary impulse that could materially change the rates narrative.

Desk risk view: SPX is holding its 200-day moving average precariously. Street gamma is meant to be very short, but vol was soggy on 11/18 after VIX expiry. With VIX in the mid 20s and Thanksgiving next week, stabilization would be a meaningful tailwind.
The desk sees a legitimate bull case for equities if rates cooperate, arguing that much of the AI concern is already in prices.

11/18 close: S&P -23bp at 7,323 with a $2.1bn market-on-close imbalance to buy. NDX +42bp at 27,116, R2K +54bp at 2,716, Dow -111bp at 50,198. VIX 24.52, WTI $82.94, US 10Y 5.06%, gold 3,725, DXY 103.78, Bitcoin $62,467.

NVDA finished -3% after being +2% pre-market despite a beat and raise. Flows were hedge fund buying/covering against continued long-only supply, and the desk sees little real sponsorship while uncertainty persists.

Consumer names rallied on slightly better earnings (TGT +5%, TJX +9%, LOW +70bp despite a miss). Retailers had a top-5 session YTD, which the desk attributes partly to a positioning unwind after consumer was among the most net-sold sectors month to date.
Floor activity was 4 on a 1-10 scale. Asset manager flows were modestly muted and hedge funds were small net buyers via macro products. ETFs were 35% of tape vs a 28% YTD average.

PANW rose 8% after hours (after +10% in the session). F1Q headline growth accelerated y/y (total revenue and NGS ARR) but the company maintained FY RPO, operating margin and FCF margin guidance rather than raising them, against a raised revenue/NGS outlook.

The desk read the Fed minutes as slightly more dovish than headlines. A couple of participants said a move of more than 25bp could warrant consideration at the next meeting, conditional on unfavorable incoming inflation data.

Derivatives desk: S&P traded in a spot-down, vol-down regime as negative sentiment and the post-earnings NVDA reversal weighed. Vol compressed after VIX expiry and NVDA earnings without equities getting a meaningful bid, which the desk calls arguably more concerning. A customer bought 52.5k NVDA Feb call spreads. S&P implied move through the end of the week and Nov regular expiry is 1.55%.
ES1 top-of-book depth averaged $4.2m at the touch, one of the worst liquidity sessions in four years, which exacerbates price moves.
Watch list for 11/19: Walmart earnings, jobless claims, Philly Fed, the 10-year TIPS auction at 18:00, and JPY approaching 160.
